title: Batch attack/block decisions render as '(no response)' in blunder analysis, causing false-positive annotations
description:
In `puppeteer/src/puppeteer/decision_renderer.py:345-352`, `_chosen_display()` returns `"(no response)"` when `chosen is None`, without checking `chosen_args` for batch attack/block data.

For batch attack declarations (`choose_action(attackers=[...])`) and batch block declarations (`choose_action(blockers=[...])`), the `chosen` field is `None` because the response uses `chosenArgs` instead of a simple index. But `_chosen_display` ignores `chosenArgs` entirely and returns `"(no response)"`.

The blunder analysis LLM (Opus 4.6) sees `"Chosen: (no response)"` and concludes the player timed out and failed to declare attackers/blockers. This produces completely false annotations claiming missed attacks that actually happened.

Evidence from `game_20260228_172012_g3`:
- 5 out of 9 annotations are false positives caused by this bug
- 3 are labeled "major" severity, including one claiming "missed lethal" on a turn where the player attacked with all creatures and won
- All 5 false annotations follow the pattern: decision has `chosen=None, chosenArgs={"attackers":[...]}`, renderer shows `"(no response)"`, LLM concludes player timed out

Affected decisions in this game:
- Decision 27: Haiku attacked with Nocturnal Feeder → annotated as "failed to attack"
- Decision 36: Grok4 attacked with Ravenous Giant → annotated as "failed to attack" 
- Decision 46: Haiku attacked with all 4 creatures → annotated as "failed to attack"
- Decision 51: Grok4 attacked with Ravenous Giant → annotated as "failed to attack"
- Decision 65: Haiku attacked with all for lethal → annotated as "timed out, missed lethal"

Source: `puppeteer/src/puppeteer/decision_renderer.py:345-352` — `_chosen_display()` receives `chosen_args` as a parameter but never uses it when `chosen is None`.

Suggested fix: Before returning `"(no response)"`, check `chosen_args` for `attackers` or `blockers` keys and render those. E.g.:
- `{"attackers": ["all"]}` → `"Attack with all creatures"`
- `{"attackers": ["p20"]}` → `"Attack with Ravenous Giant"` (resolve name from choices)
- `{"blockers": ["p5:p1"]}` → `"Block with ..."` (resolve names)

This likely affects every game analyzed by the blunder pipeline — any game with batch attacks or blocks will have false-positive annotations.
